statements.label: supported
statements.text: The blue-petal water lily Nymphaea colorata has a sequenced genome of 409 megabases.
statements.evidence: Here we report the 409-megabase genome sequence of the blue-petal water lily (Nymphaea colorata).
statements.note: The abstract reports a 409-megabase genome sequence for the blue-petal water lily N. colorata.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: In N. colorata, the putative floral scent biosynthetic genes are expressed mainly in the petals rather than in the leaves.
statements.evidence: Water lilies have evolved attractive floral scents and colours, which are features shared with mesangiosperms, and we identified their putative biosynthetic genes in N. colorata.
statements.note: The abstract says putative biosynthetic genes for floral scents and colours were identified, but reports nothing about the tissues in which they are expressed.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: According to the phylogenomic analyses, Amborellales split off earlier than Nymphaeales, the two forming successive sister lineages to all other living angiosperms.
statements.evidence: Our phylogenomic analyses support Amborellales and Nymphaeales as successive sister lineages to all other extant angiosperms.
statements.note: Successive sister lineages listed as Amborellales then Nymphaeales means Amborellales branched off first and Nymphaeales next, before all other extant angiosperms.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Genes kept after the Nymphaealean whole-genome duplication include homologues of regulators of the flowering transition and of flower development.
statements.evidence: Among the genes retained from this whole-genome duplication are homologues of genes that regulate flowering transition and flower development.
statements.note: The abstract lists homologues of flowering-transition and flower-development regulators among the genes retained from the Nymphaealean whole-genome duplication.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The results suggest that the ancestral land plant was more complex than had been assumed from topologies placing liverworts as sister to all other embryophytes.
statements.evidence: Our results imply that the ancestral embryophyte was more complex than has been envisaged based on topologies recognizing liverworts as the sister lineage to all other embryophytes.
statements.note: The abstract states that the results imply a more complex ancestral embryophyte than envisaged under topologies with liverworts as sister to all other embryophytes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Of the 15 distinct rooted relationships considered for embryophytes, the analyses rejected all except three, and those three differ only in where hornworts sit.
statements.evidence: Of the 15 distinct rooted relationships for embryophytes, we reject all but three hypotheses, which differ only in the position of hornworts.
statements.note: The abstract states that all but three of the 15 rooted embryophyte hypotheses were rejected and that the remaining three differ only in the position of hornworts.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Molecular clock analyses in the study date the origin of land plants to the Cambrian period.
statements.evidence: diminishes inconsistency between phylogeny and the fossil record
statements.note: The abstract discusses how the phylogeny fits the fossil record but reports no molecular dating of when land plants originated.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Bayesian supertree estimation from gene trees recovered bryophytes as a monophyletic group.
statements.evidence: Both maximum-likelihood analyses that compare the fit of each gene tree to proposed species trees and Bayesian supertree estimation based on gene trees support bryophyte monophyly.
statements.note: Bayesian supertree estimation based on gene trees is one of the analyses the abstract says supported bryophyte monophyly.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The Anthoceros genomes are smaller than the genomes of most mosses and liverworts.
statements.evidence: The Anthoceros genomes lack repeat-dense centromeres as well as whole-genome duplication, and contain a limited transcription factor repertoire.
statements.note: The abstract describes the centromeres, the absence of whole-genome duplication and the transcription factor repertoire of the Anthoceros genomes, but gives no genome sizes or size comparisons.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study provides three high-quality genome sequences from hornworts of the genus Anthoceros.
statements.evidence: Here, we provide three high-quality genomes of Anthoceros hornworts.
statements.note: The abstract states that three high-quality Anthoceros hornwort genomes are provided.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Several Anthoceros genes linked to meristem and stomatal function in angiosperms are upregulated as the sporophyte develops.
statements.evidence: Several genes involved in angiosperm meristem and stomatal function are conserved in Anthoceros and upregulated during sporophyte development
statements.note: The abstract reports that several genes involved in angiosperm meristem and stomatal function are upregulated during Anthoceros sporophyte development.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: LCIB, a carbon-concentrating mechanism gene from Chlamydomonas, occurs in hornworts but is missing from other plant lineages.
statements.evidence: found that LCIB, a Chlamydomonas CCM gene, is present in hornworts but absent in other plant lineages
statements.note: The abstract states that the Chlamydomonas CCM gene LCIB is present in hornworts and absent in other plant lineages.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study finds evidence for two separate whole-genome duplications in ferns, one at the base of the core leptosporangiates and one unique to Azolla.
statements.evidence: present evidence for episodic whole-genome duplication in ferns-one at the base of 'core leptosporangiates' and one specific to Azolla
statements.note: The abstract presents evidence for two whole-genome duplications in ferns, one at the base of the core leptosporangiates and one specific to Azolla.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Azolla and its nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterial partners show a clear pattern of cospeciation.
statements.evidence: Azolla coexists in a unique symbiosis with N 2 -fixing cyanobacteria, and we demonstrate a clear pattern of cospeciation between the two partners.
statements.note: The abstract states that a clear pattern of cospeciation was demonstrated between Azolla and its N2-fixing cyanobacteria.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The Azolla genome is missing genes that arbuscular mycorrhizal and root nodule symbioses have in common.
statements.evidence: the Azolla genome lacks genes that are common to arbuscular mycorrhizal and root nodule symbioses
statements.note: The abstract reports that the Azolla genome lacks genes common to arbuscular mycorrhizal and root nodule symbioses.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The Azolla filiculoides genome is smaller than the Salvinia cucullata genome.
statements.evidence: Ferns are the closest sister group to all seed plants, yet little is known about their genomes other than that they are generally colossal.
statements.note: The abstract says fern genomes are generally colossal but gives no genome sizes for Azolla or Salvinia and does not compare the two.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: About one-quarter of each salmonid genome evolved under LORe, with rediploidization and functional divergence arising repeatedly and independently, more than 50 million years after the WGD.
statements.evidence: One-quarter of each salmonid genome, harbouring at least 4550 ohnologues, has evolved under LORe, with rediploidization and functional divergence occurring on multiple independent occasions >50 million years post-WGD.
statements.note: The abstract reports that one-quarter of each salmonid genome evolved under LORe, with rediploidization and divergence occurring independently more than 50 million years post-WGD.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The delay in salmonid rediploidization was caused by bursts of transposable element activity after the whole-genome duplication.
statements.evidence: Salmonid fish, whose ancestor underwent WGD by autotetraploidization ~95 million years ago, fit such a 'time-lag' model of post-WGD radiation, which occurred alongside a major delay in the rediploidization process.
statements.note: The abstract describes a major delay in rediploidization but does not name any cause for it.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Many LORe ohnologues show regulatory divergence and have functions in lineage-specific physiological adaptations.
statements.evidence: We demonstrate the existence and regulatory divergence of many LORe ohnologues with functions in lineage-specific physiological adaptations
statements.note: The abstract states that many LORe ohnologues show regulatory divergence and have functions in lineage-specific physiological adaptations.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Compared with older ohnologues that started diverging in the salmonid ancestor, LORe ohnologues are enriched for a different set of functions.
statements.evidence: We show that LORe ohnologues are enriched for different functions than 'older' ohnologues that began diverging in the salmonid ancestor.
statements.note: The abstract reports that LORe ohnologues are enriched for different functions than the older ohnologues that began diverging in the salmonid ancestor.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Sterlet proteins evolve at a very low rate, no faster than in other deep vertebrate branches such as the coelacanth.
statements.evidence: Our analysis revealed a very low protein evolution rate that is at least as slow as in other deep branches of the vertebrate tree, such as that of the coelacanth.
statements.note: The abstract reports a very low protein evolution rate in the sterlet, at least as slow as in deep vertebrate branches such as the coelacanth.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The sterlet genome revealed a whole-genome duplication dating to the Jurassic, early in the evolution of the whole sturgeon lineage.
statements.evidence: We uncovered a whole-genome duplication that occurred in the Jurassic, early in the evolution of the entire sturgeon lineage.
statements.note: The abstract reports a Jurassic whole-genome duplication early in the evolution of the entire sturgeon lineage.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The sterlet genome has a lower transposable element content than typical teleost fish genomes.
statements.evidence: The archaic characteristics of this ancient fish lineage place it in a key phylogenetic position at the base of the ~30,000 modern teleost fish species.
statements.note: The abstract places sturgeons at the base of the teleosts but reports nothing about transposable element content in either.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Known adaptive processes have helped the sturgeon genome keep a high degree of structural and functional tetraploidy for more than 180 million years.
statements.evidence: While known adaptive processes helped conserve a high degree of structural and functional tetraploidy over more than 180 million years
statements.note: The abstract states that known adaptive processes helped conserve a high degree of structural and functional tetraploidy over more than 180 million years.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The second diploid progenitor of C. carpio, apart from the Barbinae lineage, has since gone extinct.
statements.evidence: We identify a Barbinae lineage as potential diploid progenitor of C. carpio
statements.note: The abstract identifies a Barbinae lineage as a potential diploid progenitor but says nothing about the fate of the other progenitor.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across the surveyed tissues, gene expression from homoeologues is biased, with subgenome B more dominant than the other subgenome.
statements.evidence: Instead, we find gene expression bias across surveyed tissues such that subgenome B is more dominant in homoeologous expression.
statements.note: The abstract reports an expression bias across surveyed tissues in which subgenome B is more dominant in homoeologous expression.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Common carp's two diploid progenitors are estimated to have split roughly 23 million years ago and to have combined roughly 12.4 million years ago.
statements.evidence: We estimate that the two diploid progenitors diverged around 23 Mya and merged around 12.4 Mya based on the divergence rates of homoeologous genes and transposable elements in two subgenomes.
statements.note: The abstract estimates the divergence of the two progenitors at around 23 Mya and their merger at around 12.4 Mya.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Neither subgenome of allotetraploid C. carpio has undergone extensive gene loss.
statements.evidence: No extensive gene losses are observed in either subgenome.
statements.note: The abstract states that no extensive gene losses were observed in either subgenome.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Regulatory genes are enriched in the intermediate class of angiosperm core gene families.
statements.evidence: The intermediate class was overrepresented in regulatory genes
statements.note: The abstract reports that the intermediate class of gene families was overrepresented in regulatory genes.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Gene families that are single-copy across flowering plants are also kept as single copies in animal genomes.
statements.evidence: For most gene families, we observe a strikingly consistent pattern of gene duplicability across species, with gene families being either primarily single-copy or multicopy in all species.
statements.note: The abstract reports consistent duplicability only across the 37 flowering plant species studied and says nothing about animal genomes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Gene families in the intermediate class are often retained in duplicate for tens of millions of years after whole-genome duplication but eventually revert largely to single copies.
statements.evidence: An intermediate class contains gene families that are often retained in duplicate for periods extending to tens of millions of years after whole-genome duplication, but ultimately appear to be largely restored to singleton status
statements.note: The abstract describes the intermediate class as often retained in duplicate for tens of millions of years after whole-genome duplication before largely returning to singleton status.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Single-copy gene families mainly function in genome stability and organelle function, while multicopy families mainly function in signaling, transport and metabolism.
statements.evidence: with single-copy genes being mainly involved in the maintenance of genome stability and organelle function and multicopy genes in signaling, transport, and metabolism
statements.note: The abstract assigns genome stability and organelle function to single-copy genes and signaling, transport and metabolism to multicopy genes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The ortholog sets indicate that the last eukaryotic common ancestor already had a complex kinetochore.
statements.evidence: The resulting ortholog sets imply that the last eukaryotic common ancestor (LECA) possessed a complex kinetochore
statements.note: The abstract states that the ortholog sets imply a complex kinetochore in the last eukaryotic common ancestor.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Kinetochores diverged more often through gene loss and duplication than through invention and displacement.
statements.evidence: These kinetochores diverged through gene loss, duplication, and, less frequently, invention and displacement.
statements.note: The abstract lists gene loss and duplication as routes of kinetochore divergence, with invention and displacement occurring less frequently.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The survey covered 90 phylogenetically diverse eukaryotes and traced orthologs of 70 kinetochore proteins in them.
statements.evidence: we determined orthologs of 70 kinetochore proteins in 90 phylogenetically diverse eukaryotes
statements.note: The abstract reports that orthologs of 70 kinetochore proteins were determined in 90 phylogenetically diverse eukaryotes.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Kinetochore proteins are lost most often in parasitic eukaryotic lineages.
statements.evidence: The extensive diversity of kinetochore compositions in eukaryotes poses numerous questions regarding evolutionary flexibility of essential cellular functions.
statements.note: The abstract notes extensive diversity of kinetochore composition but does not relate gene losses to parasitism or any other lifestyle.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The A. japonicus genome assembly is about 805 Mb and contains 30,350 protein-coding genes.
statements.evidence: to achieve an assembly of approximately 805 Mb (contig N50 of 190 Kb and scaffold N50 of 486 Kb), with 30,350 protein-coding genes and high continuity
statements.note: The abstract reports an assembly of approximately 805 Mb with 30,350 protein-coding genes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Analyses of organ regrowth after evisceration point to a significantly expanded fibrinogen-related protein (FREP) gene family in sea cucumber visceral regeneration.
statements.evidence: provided insight into the molecular underpinnings of visceral regeneration, including a specific tandem-duplicated prostatic secretory protein of 94 amino acids (PSP94)-like gene family and a significantly expanded fibrinogen-related protein (FREP) gene family
statements.note: The abstract names a significantly expanded FREP gene family among the findings on visceral regeneration from analyses of organ regrowth after evisceration.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The A. japonicus genome carries fewer Hox genes than the genomes of sea urchins.
statements.evidence: The unique shape and weak mineralization of the sea cucumber adult body were also preliminarily explained by the contraction of biomineralization genes.
statements.note: The abstract links body shape and weak mineralization to contracted biomineralization genes but does not mention Hox genes or compare sea cucumbers with sea urchins.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Marker genes associated with the notochord and gill slits are present in the sea cucumber genome.
statements.evidence: Phylogenetic and comparative genomic analyses revealed the presence of marker genes associated with notochord and gill slits
statements.note: The abstract reports that phylogenetic and comparative genomic analyses revealed marker genes associated with notochord and gill slits.
